Paint one illustration of a single moment from The Holy Bible.

RULES (they outrank everything below):
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) A subject without form is never drawn. Only the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind the moment names may stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the moment names who sits on it.
8) A character you draw from CANON keeps exactly that look. Anyone else the moment needs appears as an unnamed figure with an ordinary, different face.

MOMENT (Leviticus 1:16): "and he shall take away its crop and its feathers, and cast it beside the altar on the east part, in the place of the ashes."

CONTEXT (for understanding only; paint the moment above):
- Before: The priest shall bring it to the altar, and wring off its head, and burn it on the altar; and its blood shall be drained out on the side of the altar;
- After: He shall tear it by its wings, but shall not divide it apart. The priest shall burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the presence.

HOW TO READ IT: choose the single instant that best shows what happens in the moment and paint that, as if the viewer stands inside the scene. When someone speaks, show the speaker and listeners where they are; never paint the content of the speech as a separate scene or as figures beside them. Figures of speech and comparisons are not literal objects. Infer place, time, light and weather from the text and context.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. the presence is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement
People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples.
Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments.
Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.
Technology: Bronze tools, chariots and early iron; no modern objects.

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the moment are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

IMAGERY, NOT FORM (binding): wherever the text calls something "the presence", it has no body. Words that give it a seat, clothing, hair, face, hands, feet or a figure are imagery: paint none of them, not even as light or cloud in that shape. Show the place, the people who witness it, and the light, fire, cloud or wind spread through the place; any throne, seat or chariot stays empty.

CANON, NAMED HERE (fixed look; the moment decides pose, expression, clothing changes and action):
- the altar: a square hearth of acacia wood overlaid with bronze, set in an open courtyard before the tent door, with projecting horns at its four corners and a fire burning continually upon it; a bronze basin and its base stand near; the ground at its base is worn and ash-grey; a tent of linen hangings rises behind it in the desert.

CANON, ELSEWHERE IN THIS PASSAGE (draw one only when the moment involves them, for example as "he" or "they"; otherwise leave them out):
- Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.
- The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.
- The tabernacle: a portable sanctuary of a rectangular tent of fine twined linen curtains in blue, purple and scarlet woven with cherubim, over a covering of goats' hair and rams' skins, stretched over upright acacia boards overlaid with gold, set in silver sockets and held by gold-covered bars, enclosed by a court of white linen hangings on bronze pillars.

ART STYLE: Fresco
Rendering: A finished early Renaissance fresco-style painting of the work's world: calm, monumental figures, clear gestures and simple architecture, painted in soft matte color.
Palette: Soft earth reds, ochres, sage greens and pale lapis blue on light grounds.
Lighting: Even, gentle daylight with soft modelling and few cast shadows.
Materials and texture: Matte, chalky paint surface within the depicted world.
Composition: Balanced, legible staging with figures in a shallow space; the scene painted out to every edge and corner.
Negatives: Show the scene itself, never a wall, plaster cracks, painted border, frame or ornamental band. No letters or inscriptions anywhere, and halos, if any, are plain. Avoid photorealism and cartoon caricature.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached in this order; identity and rendering only, never composition):
- Image 1: Moses's reference sheet (one figure in several views). Keep Moses's identity exactly; do not copy its poses, layout or plain background.
- Image 2: The tabernacle's reference sheet (views of one place or thing). Keep The tabernacle's identity exactly; do not copy its poses, layout or plain background.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted differently.

Rendering: Pen-and-ink drawing with transparent watercolor washes laid over the whole picture; a finished watercolor painting of the work's world, not a sketch.

Lighting: Clear natural light; shadows as cool layered washes.
Materials and texture: Confident ink linework, wet-in-wet blooms and granulating pigment within the depicted world.
Composition: A complete scene: setting, sky and ground painted out to every edge and corner, with detail concentrated on key subjects.
Negatives: Washes, pigment and scenery must reach every edge. No white or cream paper margins, unpainted corners, paper edges, sketchbook, tape, border or vignette.
